newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli shekel surges against dollar.
newsitem.headline: Israeli shekel surges against dollar.

text.p: The Israeli shekel's representative rate was fixed sharply higher against the dollar on Monday after the U.S. currency plunged in Asia, dealers said.
"The shekel rose sharply against the dollar today after the U.S. currency dropped abroad," said Zahi Elias of Bank Leumi.

Speculation that Japan's trade surplus will be discussed by the Group of Seven (G7) leading industrial nations next week drove the dollar down more than two yen in Asian trade to 111.80, its weakest since November 25, 1996.

Elias said that the decline of the dollar pushed the basket downwards forcing the Bank of Israel to intervene in the market. "The central bank was acting on a relatively high scale today buying more than $150 million to support the basket," he said.
The central bank has been intervening regularly in the market to support the currency basket, which has been trading at the bottom end of its trading band since the start of the year.
"Volume was relatively high today because there will be no trading on Wednesday," Elias said.
The Bank of Israel will not set a representative rate on Wednesday because of the Jewish holiday of Shavuot.

The representative rate for the dollar was fixed at 3.4010 shekels, against 3.4150 on Friday. The basket, composed of the dollar, mark, sterling, French franc and yen, was fixed at 3.7021 against 3.7009 on Friday.
On the crosses, the shekel traded against the yen at 3.0224 shekels per 100 yen compared with 2.9502 on Friday, and against the mark at 1.9842 shekels compared with 1.9748 on Friday.
In late afternoon, the dollar was trading at 3.4020 shekels.
- Dan Gerstenfeld, Tel Aviv newsroom, 972-3-537-2211 x233
